stories.title: NLCS Game 3 Recap — Dodgers 3, Brewers 1; Snell Answers the Call
stories.angle: Blake Snell delivered exactly what the Dodgers needed — a dominant outing in a must-win Game 3 at Dodger Stadium. LA won 3-1, with the bullpen using four relievers to get the final 10 outs. The Brewers still lead the NLCS 2-1, but the series is alive. Game 4 is Thursday at 9 PM ET on FS1 with Tyler Glasnow expected to start for Los Angeles.

stories.title: ALCS Game 2 Recap — Peralta Gem, Ramirez Error Sink Guardians 3-1; Series Tied 1-1
stories.angle: Freddy Peralta threw a gem — 6 scoreless innings, 6 strikeouts — and all three Tampa Bay runs came courtesy of a critical Jose Ramirez error in the 4th inning. A ground ball hit the turf seam and rolled through Ramirez's legs; Liam Hicks followed with a 2-run single and three unearned runs crossed. Rays 3, Guardians 1. Series tied 1-1. Game 3 is Thursday Oct. 15 at 6 PM ET at Progressive Field.

stories.title: Ohtani's October Disappearing Act — .150 Average, 0 HR Since August
stories.angle: Shohei Ohtani is hitting .150 in the 2026 postseason (3-for-20), with 7 strikeouts, 0 home runs, and a .411 OPS. He hasn't homered since August 18 in Colorado. Despite discussion about benching him, manager Dave Roberts kept him in Game 3's lineup. Ohtani has been managing left knee and biceps discomfort for three months. The biggest offensive weapon in baseball has gone missing at the worst possible moment.

stories.title: McClanahan's Postseason Is Over — What Tampa Bay Loses Without Its Ace
stories.angle: Shane McClanahan is out for the rest of the postseason with a forearm injury. The Rays ace was a key part of Tampa's rotation plan entering October. His loss now falls on arms like Peralta (six scoreless innings in Game 2) and the rest of a bullpen that has been up to the challenge. This is one of the most significant injury stories of the 2026 playoffs.

x_posts.text:
